title: Cloud Connector on Azure: internal load balancer, health probe and Gateway Load Balancer
aliases: azure gateway load balancer cloud connector
azure public load balancer cloud connector

prose.text: Workload traffic reaches Azure Cloud Connectors through an internal Standard load balancer that health-probes each connector; newer reference modules add a Gateway Load Balancer path for inbound inspection. The values below are the reference module's defaults.

prose.label: The probe Cloud Connector answers.
prose.text: The probe contract (the ?cchealth path, 200 for healthy, 503 or silence for unhealthy) is in [[cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing:cchealth-path]] and [[cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing:health-codes]]; what happens to sessions on a connector that turns unhealthy is [[cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing:unhealthy-sessions]].

prose.label: Changing the defaults.
prose.text: Help's 15-second Azure default and its advice to involve Support before changing it are [[cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing:probe-intervals]] and [[cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing:change-via-support]].

prose.label: Availability zones.
prose.text: The two-per-zone recommendation is [[cloud-connector.overview.load-balancing:az-recommendation]]. One NAT gateway per zone is in [[cloud-connector.azure.network]]; one scale set per zone is in [[cloud-connector.azure.vmss]].

prose.heading: Gateway Load Balancer and Public Load Balancer

prose.text: {{gwlb-purpose}} {{gwlb-module}} {{public-lb-modes}} {{gwlb-byo-out-of-scope}} The examples that use these modules, and their FIPS gap, are in [[cloud-connector.azure.terraform-modules]].

checks.do: Whether the load balancer probe targets the same HTTP port the connectors were provisioned with, on the /?cchealth path.
How many consecutive probes the load balancer needs to remove and to restore a connector, from probe_threshold and number_of_probes on the deployed probe.
Whether failing sessions started on a connector that was then marked unhealthy, which Help says can fail until the flow ages out.

ilb-standard.statement: The load balancer module creates a Standard SKU internal load balancer whose frontend takes a dynamic private IP in the given subnet and is zone-redundant across zones 1, 2 and 3 unless a single zone is specified.

quotes: sku = "Standard"
private_ip_address_allocation = "dynamic"

frontend_zone_specific = length(var.zones) == 1 ? var.zones : ["1", "2", "3"] ##If user specifies a single zone number for a zones supported region set just that zone. Otherwise, set all 3 zones (zone-redundant)

ilb-probe.statement: The module's probe is HTTP on `http_probe_port` (default 50000, valid values 80 or 1024-65535) with request path /?cchealth, an interval of 15 seconds by default (minimum 5), `probe_threshold` 2 and `number_of_probes` 1.

quotes: protocol = "Http" port = var.http_probe_port request_path = "/?cchealth" interval_in_seconds = var.health_check_interval probe_threshold = var.probe_threshold number_of_probes = var.number_of_probes
default = 50000
error_message = "Input http_probe_port must be set to a single value of 80 or any number between 1024-65535."
The default value is 15, the minimum value is 5" default = 15
require the same number of successful consecutive probes to be placed back in rotation." default = 2
This values allows endpoints to be taken out of rotation faster or slower than the typical times used in Azure" default = 1

probe-threshold-meaning.statement: As the module describes them, `probe_threshold` is the number of consecutive failed probes that takes an endpoint out of rotation and the same number of consecutive successful probes needed to put it back, while `number_of_probes` is the number of unanswered probes that stops traffic to the endpoint.

quotes: The number of consecutive successful or failed probes in order to allow or deny traffic from being delivered to this endpoint.

After failing the number of consecutive probes equal to this value, the endpoint will be taken out of rotation and require the same number of successful consecutive probes to be placed back in rotation.
The number of probes where if no response, will result in stopping further traffic from being delivered to the endpoint.
variable "probe_threshold" {
variable "number_of_probes" {

ilb-rule.statement: The load-balancing rule uses protocol All with frontend and backend port 0 and floating IP enabled; `load_distribution` defaults to Default and accepts SourceIP, SourceIPProtocol or Default.

quotes: protocol = "All" frontend_port = 0 backend_port = 0
enable_floating_ip = true
description = "Azure LB load distribution method" default = "Default"
error_message = "Input load_distribution must be set to either SourceIP, SourceIPProtocol, or Default."

marketplace-lb-settings.statement: In the Azure Marketplace deployment, opting out of a load balancer is meant only for non-production environments, the HTTP probe port is 80 or 1024 to 65535 and must match an existing load balancer's, and connectors go into availability sets or availability zones.

quotes: Only select this setting when deploying in a non-production environment.
HTTP Probe Port for Load Balancer: Enter the HTTP Probe Port 80 or 1024 to 65535. If selecting an existing load balancer, ensure that the ports match.
Availability Sets and Availability Zones: Select either Availability Sets or Availability Zones.

gwlb-purpose.statement: The module changelog describes Azure Gateway Load Balancer support as enabling transparent inline inspection of ingress traffic, which the existing egress-only Private LB topology cannot do, and adds greenfield and brownfield GWLB examples and Public LB examples.

quotes: Azure Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) support for Cloud Connector — enables transparent inline inspection for ingress traffic that is not possible with the existing egress-only Private LB topology.
add: greenfield example base_cc_gwlb (CC VMs + GWLB)
add: brownfield example cc_gwlb (CC VMs + GWLB in existing VNet)
add: greenfield example base_cc_public_lb (CC VMs + standalone Public LB)

gwlb-module.statement: The GWLB module creates a Gateway SKU load balancer with a private frontend, a backend pool with internal and external VXLAN tunnel interfaces, an HTTP probe on /?cchealth and a rule, intended to be chained to a consumer Public Load Balancer whose inbound traffic is VXLAN-encapsulated through the Cloud Connectors before returning to its destination.

quotes: This module creates an Azure Gateway Load Balancer (SKU `Gateway`) with a private frontend IP, a backend address pool with dual VXLAN tunnel interfaces (internal + external), an HTTP health probe, and a load-balancing rule
The created GWLB is intended to be chained to a consumer Public Load Balancer
which encapsulates the traffic in VXLAN and forwards it to backend Cloud Connectors for inspection — before being decapsulated and returned to the original destination.
request_path = "/?cchealth"

public-lb-modes.statement: The Public Load Balancer module serves inbound DNAT (the fwd ZIA feature) either standalone, distributing to Cloud Connector NICs or scale-set instances, or as a consumer chained to the GWLB when `gateway_load_balancer_frontend_ip_configuration_id` is set; its rules enable floating IP, which DNAT for fwd ZIA requires.

quotes: to be used with Cloud Connector clusters that require inbound DNAT (e.g. the `fwd ZIA` feature).
**Standalone Public LB** — the Public IP frontend distributes inbound traffic directly to CC backend NICs (or VMSS instances).

**Consumer LB chained to a Gateway Load Balancer** — when `gateway_load_balancer_frontend_ip_configuration_id` is set, inbound traffic at the Public IP frontend is transparently redirected through the GWLB (and its CC VMs/VMSS) before reaching the original destination.
LB rules have `enable_floating_ip = true`. This is required to support DNAT for the `fwd ZIA` feature.

gwlb-byo-out-of-scope.statement: Bringing a pre-existing GWLB (or Private LB) is out of scope for the load-balancer modules; an operator with an existing GWLB wires the Cloud Connector NIC to backend-pool association outside the module.

quotes: Bringing your own (`byo_`) pre-existing GWLB is currently **out of scope** for this module. The same is true for the `terraform-zscc-lb-azure` Private LB module.
should wire the NIC → backend-pool association outside this module.
